newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE WHITE SUGAR CLAWS HIGHER, ARBITRAGE ACTIVE.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE WHITE SUGAR CLAWS HIGHER, ARBITRAGE ACTIVE.

text.p: White sugar futures finally found some strength on Thursday to break out of the week's corrective downtrend but most attention was centred on the arbitrage against New York, traders said.
Bargain-hunters of October/October supported London's nearby whites contract after persistent trade selling pressured the differential down to around $65, compared with $72 at the start of the month.
"The whites have stayed still and the attention has been on the raws -- it's unbelievable," said one trader.
Short-covering and fund buying in October raws was thought to be behind the rally to a high of 11.87 cents/lb, up 0.20 on the day.
But traders said the bubble could soon burst, especially given the hefty fund long position.
This week, the London market has tended to be extremely quiet in early trading and looking to New York to provide some boost in sentiment for the afternoon.
At 1630 GMT nearby contracts were slightly firmer, with October was up 40 cents at $325.10 and December up 80 cents at $322.50. Volume was 1,776 lots, dominated by October and March.
Trading on the Paris market was confined to just 161 lots of the two nearby contracts.
October was up 20 cents at $324.50 and December unchanged at $321.50.
